title: Essential constancy is invariant under initial restriction of pro-diagrams
statement: Let $H:\mathcal I\to\mathcal J$ be an initial functor between cofiltered categories and let $M:\mathcal J\to\mathcal C$ be a diagram in a category $\mathcal C$ [def-pc-essentially-constant-pro-diagram]. Then $M$ is essentially constant as a pro-object if and only if $M\circ H$ is essentially constant, with the same value. More precisely, if $M$ is essentially constant with value $X$ and cone maps $u_j:X\to M(j)$, then $M\circ H$ is essentially constant with value $X$ and cone maps $u_{H(i)}$; and if $M\circ H$ is essentially constant with value $X$ and cone maps $v_i:X\to M(H(i))$, then $M$ is essentially constant with value $X$ and cone maps $u_j$ satisfying $u_{H(i)}=v_i$ for all $i$.

proof.text: Comparison of Hom-colimits. Here "initial" is Stacks' notion (Categories, Definition of an initial functor): conditions (1), (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-initial-functor-limit]. Fix an object $W$ of $\mathcal C$ and consider the functor $j\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(M(j),W)$ from $\mathcal J$ to the opposite category $\mathrm{Set}^{\mathrm{op}}$; its limit in $\mathrm{Set}^{\mathrm{op}}$ is the colimit $\varinjlim_{j\in\mathcal J^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Hom}(M(j),W)$ in $\mathrm{Set}$, which exists. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-initial-functor-limit] to $H$ and this functor (with $\mathrm{Set}^{\mathrm{op}}$ as the target category) gives that the canonical map $\kappa_W:\varinjlim_{i\in\mathcal I^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Hom}(M(H(i)),W)\to\varinjlim_{j\in\mathcal J^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Hom}(M(j),W)$, $[\psi]_i\mapsto[\psi]_{H(i)}$, is a bijection.

source.place: Categories, Lemma Tag 0A1T proof: Lemma Tag 04E7 (lemma-cofinal) for the cofinal functor H^opp

proof.text: Assume $M$ is essentially constant with value $X$ and cone maps $u_j$. By [lem-pc-essentially-constant-pro-hom-colimit] the map $\varinjlim_{j}\operatorname{Hom}(M(j),W)\to\operatorname{Hom}(X,W)$, $[\psi]_j\mapsto\psi\circ u_j$, is bijective; composing with $\kappa_W$ of Step 1, the map $\beta_W:[\psi]_i\mapsto\psi\circ u_{H(i)}$ from $\varinjlim_{i\in\mathcal I^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Hom}(M(H(i)),W)$ to $\operatorname{Hom}(X,W)$ is bijective for every $W$. Let $[r']_{i_0}=\beta_X^{-1}(\mathrm{id}_X)$, with $r':M(H(i_0))\to X$; then $r'\circ u_{H(i_0)}=\mathrm{id}_X$, and $\beta_W([\varphi\circ r']_{i_0})=\varphi$, so $\varphi\mapsto[\varphi\circ r']_{i_0}$ is the inverse bijection $\beta_W^{-1}$. By [lem-pur-essential-constant-pro-criterion-05py] ($\mathcal I$ cofiltered, index $i_0$, $r=r'$), $M\circ H$ is essentially constant with value $X$, with cone maps $u'_i$ satisfying $[u'_i\circ r']_{i_0}=[\mathrm{id}_{M(H(i))}]_i$ in $\varinjlim_k\operatorname{Hom}(M(H(k)),M(H(i)))$. Applying $\beta_{M(H(i))}$ to both sides gives $u'_i\circ r'\circ u_{H(i_0)}=u_{H(i)}$, i.e. $u'_i=u_{H(i)}$: the cone maps are the restricted $u_{H(i)}$.

source.place: Categories, Lemma Tag 0A1T proof, using Lemma Tag 05PZ (2)=>(1) and (4)=>(1)

proof.text: Conversely assume $M\circ H$ is essentially constant with value $X$ and cone maps $v_i$. By [lem-pc-essentially-constant-pro-hom-colimit] (for $M\circ H$ over the cofiltered $\mathcal I$) the map $\gamma_W:[\psi]_i\mapsto\psi\circ v_i$ from $\varinjlim_{i\in\mathcal I^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Hom}(M(H(i)),W)$ to $\operatorname{Hom}(X,W)$ is bijective. Let $[r]_{i_0}=\gamma_X^{-1}(\mathrm{id}_X)$, $r:M(H(i_0))\to X$; then $r\circ v_{i_0}=\mathrm{id}_X$ and $\gamma_W^{-1}(\varphi)=[\varphi\circ r]_{i_0}$. Composing with $\kappa_W$ of Step 1, $\varphi\mapsto[\varphi\circ r]_{H(i_0)}$ is a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(X,W)\to\varinjlim_{j\in\mathcal J^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Hom}(M(j),W)$ for every $W$. By [lem-pur-essential-constant-pro-criterion-05py] (index $j_0=H(i_0)$, morphism $r$), $M$ is essentially constant with value $X$, with cone maps $u_j$ characterized by $[u_j\circ r]_{H(i_0)}=[\mathrm{id}_{M(j)}]_j$ in $\varinjlim_k\operatorname{Hom}(M(k),M(j))$.

source.place: Categories, Lemma Tag 0A1T proof, using Lemma Tag 05PZ (4)=>(1)

proof.text: The cone maps agree: for an index $i$ take $j=H(i)$ and $W=M(H(i))$ in Step 3. Both $[u_{H(i)}\circ r]_{i_0}$ and $[\mathrm{id}]_i$ in $\varinjlim_{k\in\mathcal I^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Hom}(M(H(k)),M(H(i)))$ are sent by $\kappa_W$ to the equal classes $[u_{H(i)}\circ r]_{H(i_0)}=[\mathrm{id}]_{H(i)}$; $\kappa_W$ is injective, so they are equal, and applying $\gamma_W$ gives $u_{H(i)}\circ r\circ v_{i_0}=v_i$, i.e. $u_{H(i)}=v_i$ since $r\circ v_{i_0}=\mathrm{id}_X$.

lean.statement: theorem initial_iff_essentiallyConstantProDiagram {I : Type uI} {J : Type uJ} {C : Type uC} [Category.{vI} I] [Category.{vJ} J] [Category.{vC} C] [IsCofiltered I] [IsCofiltered J] (H : I ⥤ J) [H.Initial] (M : J ⥤ C) (X : C) : (IsEssentiallyConstantProDiagram M X ↔ IsEssentiallyConstantProDiagram (H ⋙ M) X) ∧ (∀ u : (Functor.const J).obj X ⟶ M, (∃ j₀ : J, ∃ r : M.obj j₀ ⟶ X, u.app j₀ ≫ r = 𝟙 X ∧ ∀ j : J, ∃ k : J, ∃ a : k ⟶ j₀, ∃ b : k ⟶ j, M.map b = M.map a ≫ r ≫ u.app j) → ∃ i₀ : I, ∃ r : M.obj (H.obj i₀) ⟶ X, u.app (H.obj i₀) ≫ r = 𝟙 X ∧ ∀ i : I, ∃ k : I, ∃ a : k ⟶ i₀, ∃ b : k ⟶ i, M.map (H.map b) = M.map (H.map a) ≫ r ≫ u.app (H.obj i)) ∧ (∀ v : (Functor.const I).obj X ⟶ H ⋙ M, (∃ i₀ : I, ∃ r : M.obj (H.obj i₀) ⟶ X, v.app i₀ ≫ r = 𝟙 X ∧ ∀ i : I, ∃ k : I, ∃ a : k ⟶ i₀, ∃ b : k ⟶ i, M.map (H.map b) = M.map (H.map a) ≫ r ≫ v.app i) → ∃ u : (Functor.const J).obj X ⟶ M, (∃ j₀ : J, ∃ r : M.obj j₀ ⟶ X, u.app j₀ ≫ r = 𝟙 X ∧ ∀ j : J, ∃ k : J, ∃ a : k ⟶ j₀, ∃ b : k ⟶ j, M.map b = M.map a ≫ r ≫ u.app j) ∧ ∀ i : I, u.app (H.obj i) = v.app i)
